findings.title: No wire-body test that user_context reaches the MCP-Connect payload
findings.problem: The EPMCDME-13260 deliverable is that user_context (with extra_attributes stripped) is serialised into the JSON body POSTed to MCP-Connect on tools/call and tools/list. The new tests only assert MCPExecutionContext.to_request_fields() dict output (test_models.py) and masked DEBUG-log text (test_client.py TestMCPConnectClientUserContextDebugLog); none inspect post.call_args / the post_body built by _build_request_payload. MCPToolInvocationRequest.user_context (models.py:510) sits next to five sibling fields that all carry Field(exclude=True).
findings.impact: A regression that adds Field(exclude=True) to MCPToolInvocationRequest.user_context, or re-adds user_context to an exclude set at client.py:128, would stop the profile reaching MCP-Connect and silently turn EPMCDME-13260 into a no-op with the full test suite still green. The DSP path guards against the equivalent regression; the MCP path has no such assertion.
findings.recommendation: In tests/codemie/service/mcp/test_client.py, after invoke_tool(...) and list_tools(...) with an MCPExecutionContext whose user_context is set, assert post.call_args.kwargs['json']['user_context'] equals the expected non-sensitive profile dict and that 'extra_attributes' is not in it.

finding_status.notes: Fix-up adds TestMCPConnectClientUserContextWireBody in tests/codemie/service/mcp/test_client.py with test_invoke_tool_sends_user_context_without_extra_attributes (asserts wire_body['method']=='tools/call', wire_body['user_context'] equals the expected non-sensitive dict, 'extra_attributes' not in it) and test_list_tools_sends_user_context_without_extra_attributes (same for 'tools/list'). Verified against current source at HEAD: client.py builds post_body = request.model_dump(exclude_none=True) from to_request_fields() and posts client.post(mcp_url, json=post_body, ...) on both list_tools (line 167) and invoke_tool (line 246); fixtures sample_tools_response / sample_tool_invocation_response and the required mock imports are present. The requested regression guard now exists on the MCP path.
